scores:
DALE'S WALK (iPhone 13, about a minute a page)

/start/ (from the email). First screen: "Christian Knight, Baton Rouge. A website guy. Sites up in 7 to 10 days, fixed prices, I own it. $1,000 to $8,000. There's his number." Tapped: the phone number strip, then "Four fixed packages" (landed on the price board, fine), then the Smilys Softwash card. Confused by: "the systems that bring in customers" and "Automations that run while you work" (what systems?); skimmed the nine-service list, stopped reading at "Growth consulting" and "SEO & performance". Found: cost, name, local, ownership, timeline, the four steps. Not found: whether the monthly care plan is required. Would call: yes. This is the best page for him.

Home. First screen: "More customers, fewer missed calls. Websites plus the text-back thing. Same prices." The phone picture of the missed-call text made sense at once. Tapped a price row to see what is in Starter and got a "Secure checkout" payment page: suspicious, backed out. Bored through "What we do" (third time the services are listed on his route). Never reached the name: it is on the twelfth screen. Saw "Care plans ... /mo" under the prices with nothing saying it is optional. Would call: yes if he came from /start/; from Google, less sure, because nothing early says who he would be dealing with.

Pricing. First screen: "Fixed prices, published up front" and a list of every price on the page. The clearest page on the site: what each package is, how long, how many pages, how long he is supported, half now and half at launch. Tapped "Care plans" in the list. Suspicious at "or it quietly rots" followed by four monthly plans with "Start plan" buttons; the no-contract line is the last thing in the section. Did not know "CRM" or "service config". Would call: yes, to ask whether he has to take a plan.

Consulting. First screen: understood the four things it sets up; then the big button wants $350 for a "Growth Audit" right after "the first check is free". Scrolled the example week (clear, clearly marked as an example), the step-by-step pictures (clear), gave up around the calculator: the page is 16.5 screens. Monthly plans here do say "no long-term contract" right under them. Would call: not from this page; would use the phone bar's free call instead of the $350 button.

Work. "Three real sites, and one washes roofs in Baton Rouge." Tapped smilyssoftwash.com. "Card payments are being set up" read as honest. No stumble. Would call.

About. "Hi, I'm Christian." A person, local, says plainly that the domain is in my name and I can leave. "Care after launch, if you want it" answers the monthly question better than the pricing page does. No photo of him (none exists; not a finding). Would call.

Contact. Big phone number, hours, a short form, "What happens next" in three steps, "No obligation" stamp. Small stumbles: "no sales sequence", and no place or prompt to leave a number for a call back (the number above the form covers the phone person). Would call rather than fill it in.

Laptop (/, /pricing/, /consulting/ at 1280x800). Same content, nothing extra to stumble on: the home hero reads in one glance with the prices visible; the four packages line up row by row; the consulting hero has the same $350 first button.
